title: ParsiPrakashVinodVedangRai563GhaAlm3Shlf4DevanagariJyotish
shelf_note: A Devanagari manuscript leaf of a Sanskrit-medium guide to Persian verbs (Vedāṅgarāya's Pārasī-prakāśa tradition, 1643). It belongs in the Dharmartha Trust / eGangotri manuscript collection it is filed under.
structure_note: The counts disagree. There are 110 page records with OCR, but pages_count is 42. Structure says 0 pages translated, but the field says 42, and this page does have a translation. Probably a re-import or a stale count (E2), not missing pages. Only 19 pages have printed numbers, with 4 backsteps and 3 repeats. That is most likely the margin's two numerals (Devanagari folio '२४' and a later Western '14') being picked up in turn, or misread Devanagari folio numbers, not a real disorder.

pages.layout: oblong pothi leaf, single block of 11 lines, folio numeral in the left margin, CC-0 eGangotri watermark at the foot

ocr_errors.problem: bhavāmi ('I become') read as bhavāni ('let me become'). The translation inherits the wrong mood.
The scribe's ह is read as रू/रु/द throughout: 'रुनिष्यामीति', 'अरुनिष्यन्मे', 'दरुनिष्यं', 'दंत्यर्थे' for हनिष्यामि / अहनिष्यन् / हंत्यर्थे. The translator silently corrects these to han-.

ocr_errors.image: ख्वा ह शु / ख्वाह शुद (low confidence: the scribe's ख looks like रव)
ocr_errors.problem: The Persian future auxiliary khvāh- seems to be read as 'श्वा' every time it occurs, and 'शुद' as 'शृ'. The translation carries 'śvāhad'.
'in the sense of eating' read as 'in the sense of speaking'. The translator guesses 'eating' inside <unclear>.

ocr_errors.ocr: <meta>... The text appears to be a grammatical commentary or a treatise on verbal roots (dhatupatha) and their meanings.</meta>
ocr_errors.image: a Sanskrit-glossed list of Persian verb forms
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR's page description misidentifies the genre. It is metadata, not reader text.

tr_errors.source: मे शवे म भवा भो भवानीत्यर्थे मे शवे
tr_errors.english: **me-śave** is in the sense of <term>bhavāni</term> <gloss>let me become</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: The image reads bhavāmi, 'I become' (Persian mī-shavam). The English gives an imperative 'let me become', so the gloss teaches the wrong form.
The Persian khvāham shud ('I will become') is given as 'śvāham śud', carrying the OCR misreading of ख्वा. A reader who knows Persian cannot recognise the auxiliary.

tr_errors.english: **kharde** for the past <term>kīrtana</term> <gloss>telling of what was done</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: 'for the past' and the gloss 'telling of what was done' are an interpretation the line does not carry. kīrtana means mention or declaration.
The note claims to quote the original but misquotes it ('dama' for 'दय').

other.note: Several <unclear> spans contain the translator's own English guesses ('<unclear>should be</unclear>', '<unclear>eating</unclear>', '<unclear>"he will eat"</unclear>'). Others are untranslated romanised garble strings ('<unclear>"mā dhi vijñeya tatra darśake nija kṛtvanu ti dro"</unclear>') inside the reading text.

missing.english: **Me-śavem** <note>original: "me śave ma"</note> is in the sense of "we become"
missing.why: The body never says that the bold forms are Persian verbs (mī-shavam, zadan, khurdan, pukhtan, dīdan) written in Devanagari and matched to Sanskrit equivalents. Only the summary says it. Without that, the page reads as nonsense syllables.

missing.english: For "he will become" <term>bhaviṣyati</term> and the like, it is **śvāhī śud**
missing.why: The reader needs to be told that śvāh- stands for the Persian future auxiliary khvāh- ('will'), or the future forms cannot be followed.
The prefix me-/mī- is the Persian continuous/present marker. A reader cannot tell why it recurs on almost every form.

book_verdict: The page is the right leaf, and the English recovers the gist: a Sanskrit key to Persian verb forms. The OCR has systematic misreadings of this scribe's ह and ख, and some carry into the English ('bhavāni' for bhavāmi, 'śvāhad' for khvāhad). There is also one interpretive gloss. Nothing a general reader would catch on sight, apart from the inconsistent page counts.
